To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the design of the incentive is crucial for the effectiveness, sustainability and efficiency of an ex-ante evaluated policy measure.

(1) The design of an incentive can significantly contribute to the effectiveness and sustainability of the measure; (2) The efficiency of an incentive depends on the magnitude and the probability of its occurrence, with a low, certain reward being most efficient.
a high reward with a small probability of occurrence is the best design for a sustainable incentive and a low and certain amount of reward is the most effective and most efficient design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of policy incentives and their effects on behaviour.
an effective and sustainable policy measure for reducing negative externalities.
the design of an ex-ante evaluation tool to test the effects of policy measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of reward and punishment, with different probabilities and magnitudes, is most promising for a successful implementation of a policy measure to reduce externalities.
a combination of different incentives is most promising for a policy to reduce fertiliser application in palm oil production.
a high and certain reward is most effective and sustainable, but least efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a high reward with a small probability is the best option for an incentive.
the design of an incentive is crucial to its effectiveness and sustainability, and that it is possible to identify the design that is most effective and efficient ex-ante.
a reward is a better incentive than a punishment, and a low reward with certainty has the highest efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of incentives can be a crucial element of policy effectiveness.
the ex-ante design of policy instruments matters for effectiveness, sustainability and efficiency of policy instruments.
ex-ante evaluation should consider the design of the incentive and that the design of the incentives can be evaluated ex-ante.
